title: Beam Fusion claim: matched compact initializer and stage ablation
question: Does Beam Fusion improve compact-domain initialization or converged reconstruction under matched count, downstream optimizer, samples, seeds, and views, and which repair/optimization stages are necessary?
hypothesis: Beam Fusion's multi-view product geometry outperforms compact carve and bounded-random controls at initialization and retains an advantage after the same fixed-topology compact optimizer; unnecessary repair stages can be removed without degrading the frozen primary risks.
claim_boundary: Development-stage causal evidence about the named compact initializers and stage sequence on two outcome-exposed scenes. No RGB quality, general VRAM, topology-growth, surface-accuracy, or cross-dataset claim.

stages.label: Matched initializers
stages.purpose: Construct Beam, compact-carve, and calibration-bounded random initializations at identical Gaussian count.

stages.label: Repair factorial
stages.purpose: Compare no repair, corrected covariance only, and the explicitly retired opacity/appearance controls without changing means or count.

stages.label: Trainability factorial
stages.purpose: Compare all fields, means only, and means fixed under identical sampled supervision and updates.

stages.label: Containment ablation
stages.purpose: Compare no containment, post-fit containment, and containment plus means-frozen recovery.

stages.label: Matched convergence
stages.purpose: Evaluate initialization, fixed checkpoints, area under the risk curve, and the final frozen checkpoint.

comparators.label: Compact carve
comparators.purpose: Strong image-free structural initializer using the same compact fields and exact final count.

comparators.label: Calibration-bounded random
comparators.purpose: Lower-bound control with the same count, extent, optimizer, and random roots.

comparators.label: Beam without covariance repair
comparators.purpose: Tests whether the locally successful corrected covariance stage is needed downstream.

comparators.label: Beam means-only optimization
comparators.purpose: Tests whether direct fixed-topology position optimization is sufficient.

comparators.label: Beam means-fixed optimization
comparators.purpose: Tests whether Beam geometry should be preserved while only non-positional fields adapt.

comparators.label: Differentiable compact-support barrier
comparators.purpose: Tests a fixed-count push-inside alternative to the hard projected-center prune without reading masks.

primary_metrics.label: Initialization held-out compact pixel risk
primary_metrics.aggregation: paired median per view, seed, and scene

primary_metrics.label: Final held-out compact pixel risk
primary_metrics.aggregation: paired median per view, seed, and scene

primary_metrics.label: Final held-out compact area risk
primary_metrics.aggregation: paired median per view, seed, and scene

primary_metrics.label: Compact-risk curve area
primary_metrics.aggregation: trapezoidal checkpoint AUC, paired median over seeds and scenes

primary_metrics.label: Paired seed wins
primary_metrics.aggregation: Beam wins against the strongest comparator on both primary risks

primary_metrics.label: Projected-center containment violation
primary_metrics.aggregation: maximum over fitting views, seeds, and scenes

primary_metrics.label: Peak CUDA allocated
primary_metrics.aggregation: median over measured repeats, seeds, and scenes

resource_protocol.scope: fresh compact-only process per arm from compact manifest open through final checkpoint save
resource_protocol.aggregation: paired median on one idle named GPU; retain every raw repeat and report min/max

blockers: Reduce the prior exploratory carrier arms to the frozen factorial above and implement one task-specific runner.
Freeze equal-count compact-carve and bounded-random initialization details before changing status to ready.
Freeze an effect floor and multiplicity rule without looking at new task outcomes.
Add an outcome-unseen scene before promoting a general Beam Fusion claim.
